scenario: Greeting someone for the first time
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hello! My name is Ana.
dialogue.translation: ¡Hola! Che nombre Ana.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hi, Ana. Nice to meet you. I am Carlos.
dialogue.translation: ¡Hola, Ana! Mba'éichapa ndive. Che Carlos.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Nice to meet you too. This is my friend, Luis.
dialogue.translation: Mba'éichapa ndive avei. Ko'áĝa che mbaraka, Luis.

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: Hello, Luis. I am from Spain.
dialogue.translation: ¡Hola, Luis! Che ha'e España-gua.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: And I am from Mexico. Welcome!
dialogue.translation: Ha che ha'e México-gua. Mba'éichapa!

scenario: Asking where something is in a store
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Morfema verbal de tercera persona singular del verbo 'to be'.
Pronombre para referirse a algo ya mencionado.
Mueble o superficie horizontal para colocar cosas.
En contexto de tienda, significa 'japo' o 'jeike'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, where is the bread?
dialogue.translation: ¡Ha’ekuéra! mba’épe oiko chévere?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It is over there, on that shelf.
dialogue.translation: Oiko upépe, pe tendápe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is it right there?
dialogue.translation: Oiko upépe jey?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes. You need to get it from the top.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e. Ne ne ko’ág̃a jeike umi ári.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thank you!
dialogue.translation: ¡Aguyje!

scenario: Ordering a drink at a café
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What can I get for you?
dialogue.translation: Máva aipo ndeve?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Can I have a coffee, please?
dialogue.translation: ¿Poder aipo kafe, por favor?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hot or cold?
dialogue.translation: Tata o tata y̌?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hot, please. And what tea do you have?
dialogue.translation: Tata, por favor. Ha máva té ndeve oiko?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Here you go. Your coffee and tea.
dialogue.translation: Amo ndeve. nde kafe ha té.

key_phrases.phrase: What can I get for you?

scenario: Buying a ticket at a station
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want one ticket to London, please.
dialogue.translation: Ñeha’arõ peteĩ tiquete a Londres, porã.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: For today, with the train now?
dialogue.translation: ¿Porã ko áĝa, ndive oiko trén áĝa?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, but very early, and then I go to work.
dialogue.translation: Héve, pero ete áĝa, ha upéi aiko ajopyta.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: OK, you have the train at six. That is good.
dialogue.translation: Mba’eichapa, oiko tréni hora seis. Upéa porã.

scenario: Checking in at a hotel reception
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Good evening. Do you have a reservation?
dialogue.translation: ¡Mba’eichapa! ¿Oñemohenda piko nde?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, we have a room for two nights.
dialogue.translation: Ñande oñemohenda kuárapa peteĩ ára mbýpe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Here is your key. Your room is on the third floor.
dialogue.translation: Aje kuévo nde taguapu. nde kuárapa oikópa pýso mbohapype.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thank you. We need help with our bags.
dialogue.translation: Aguyje. Ñande ñeikotevẽ mba’éicha ñande ajaka.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Of course. How long do you want to stay?
dialogue.translation: Iporãite. Mba’éicha ojehechakuaa piko nde?

key_phrases.phrase: How long do you want to stay?

scenario: Meeting a new neighbor
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha haguã mba’épa oiko nde resa.
Ojehecha haguã mba’épa oiko nde resa.
Ko ápe, 'move' oñe’ẽ haguã mba’épa oñemboaje’ỹma.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hi! I see you just moved into the house next door.
dialogue.translation: ¡Mba’eichapa! Ahecha ko kuehe ogapy’o pe ogapy’i.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I live here now. It is my new home.
dialogue.translation: Heta, ñemohenda ko’ápe. Ko ogapy tova’ekue.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That is great! So, do you need help with your things today?
dialogue.translation: ¡Heta! Upéicha, ¿ndepyta mba’eve árape?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Maybe later. Oh, the door is open. Let me close it.
dialogue.translation: Iporã avei. ¡Oh, ogapy’i oñembota’ỹ! Añembotavy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: No problem. I am at home all morning. Come by any time.
dialogue.translation: Ndaikotevẽi. Añemohenda ko’ápe árape. Eju peve.

scenario: Asking the time on the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ko ápe, 'Do you have the time?' = ¿Tenderä nde hora?
Ko ápe, 'Can you tell me...' = ¿Nde ikatu nde ñe’ẽ...?
Oñe’ẽ hagua ojehechávo mba’eve ko ára.
Ko ápe, 'see you then' = rojojaha upéi.
Oñe’ẽ hagua ojehechávo mba’eve: 'at three' = pe mbohapy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, do you have the time?
dialogue.translation: Mba’éichapa, ¿tenderä nde hora?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sorry, I don't know. I don't have a watch.
dialogue.translation: Maitei, ndaikuaái. Ndaijapóiva che relojo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Oh, but can you tell me if it's late?
dialogue.translation: Ah, ¿ndéve ikatu nde ñe’ẽ ha’e oi tarde?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I think it's about three now.
dialogue.translation: Aju, ojehechávo mbohapy ápe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thank you! See you at three then.
dialogue.translation: Aguai! Rojojaha pe mbohapy upéi.

scenario: At the doctor for a basic checkup
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha haguã oime piko nde mba'e rehe.
Oñemoñe'ẽ haguã tembi'u oñembohetave ha oñembohetave'i.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: How do you feel today?
dialogue.translation: ¿Mba'eicha nde reikuaa ko ára?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Not better than yesterday. I have some pain here.
dialogue.translation: Ndaikuaái porãve ko'ára. Añe'ẽ mba'e'i ko ápe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: You should take this medicine. All is fine, but rest more.
dialogue.translation: Reikotevẽta nde rembi'u ko'ág̃a. Opáichagua porã, ha nde reikuaa mba'eve.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: How much do I take each day?
dialogue.translation: Mba'eicha ndohechápa ndéve ko'ág̃a?

scenario: Paying at a supermarket checkout
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Mba'éichapa ojejapo hese: cantidad total a pagar
Mba'éichapa ojejapo hese: costo de un artículo
Ñe'ẽ rehegua ojejapo hese: dinero que se devuelve al pagar de más
Ñe'ẽ rehegua ojejapo hese: comprobante de compra
Ñe'ẽ rehegua ojejapo hese: indica lugar
Ñe'ẽ rehegua ojejapo hese: en 'out of' (de) – cantidad de algo

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: That is the total. The price is twenty dollars.
dialogue.translation: Ko'ág̃a oguerekóva pe total. Pe price oguerekóva 20 dólares.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: OK. How much does it cost? Can I pay with a card?
dialogue.translation: ¡Jahéi! ¿Mba'éichapa oguerekóva pe cost? ¿Aipotápa che aheja pe card?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Yes, here is the card machine. And here is your receipt.
dialogue.translation: ¡Ha'evéi! Ko'ág̃a oguerekóva pe card machine. Ha ko'ág̃a oguerekóva nde receipt.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Thank you. I am out of cash, so card is good.
dialogue.translation: ¡Aguijey! Che ndaipóri che cash, upéi card oiko porã.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Here is your change. Have a nice day!
dialogue.translation: Ko'ág̃a oguerekóva nde change. ¡Jajokuaa porã nde ára!

scenario: Calling a friend to make simple plans
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ñe'ẽ poravopyre ojeikuaa haguã ojehechávo mba'eve.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hi, this is me. Can you call me today?
dialogue.translation: Mba'éichapa, ko'ápe che. ¿Puedes llamarme hoy?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I can call you now. Where are you?
dialogue.translation: Heta, aipo che. ¿Mo'ãpa nde?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I am at home. Can you see me tomorrow?
dialogue.translation: Aiko yma. ¿Puedes hechame ko'ẽ?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I can see you tomorrow. Where do we meet?
dialogue.translation: Heta, aipo che ko'ẽ. ¿Mo'ãpa ñandejajapo?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Meet me on this street, near the park.
dialogue.translation: Jajapo ndéve pe kóva mba'e, yvytypegua.

scenario: Describing your family to someone
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha haguéicha oikóva tembiapo ha oñemotenondéva.
Oñe’ẽ haguéicha kuñataĩ, ndaha’éi oñemoñe’ẽ oñemotenondéva.
Oñe’ẽ haguéicha kuimba’e, ndaha’éi oñemoñe’ẽ oñemotenondéva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tell me about your family.
dialogue.translation: Ehechaukáta nde tembiapo.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I live with my mother, father, and two sisters. My brother is not at home.
dialogue.translation: Aiko ndive che sy, che túva ha kuñataĩ mboy. Che kuimba’e ndaikói ogápe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is your father old or young?
dialogue.translation: ¿Nde túva tuja ha morotĩ?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: He is not very old, but my mother is very young.
dialogue.translation: Ndaha’éi ete tuja, ha che sy ovetavy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: And your sisters? Are they young too?
dialogue.translation: ¿Ha nde kuñataĩ? ¿Ovetavy avei?

key_phrases.phrase: live with my mother and father
key_phrases.translation: aiko ndive che sy ha che túva

scenario: Asking for directions in the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, is the station far from here?
dialogue.translation: Mba'éichapa, ¿ha upéa oiko mba'éichapa oñembohetia?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No, it's near. Go straight and turn left at the next street.
dialogue.translation: Nda, oñembohetia. Eikotevẽi oiko ha oikóva oiko tendápe oñembohetia.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Go straight and turn left? Is that right?
dialogue.translation: ¿Eikotevẽi oiko ha oikóva tendápe oñembohetia? ¿Ha upéa oiko mba'éichapa?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, that's right. Then go straight again. The station is on your right.
dialogue.translation: Ha’e, upéa oiko mba’éichapa. Upéi eikotevẽi oiko avei. Ha upéa oiko tendápe oñembohetia.

scenario: On a bus asking the driver for help
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ojeikuaa haguéva ojehechávo tapykue pe ógape.
Ko ápe, 'get off' oñe'ẽ joko haguéva.
Ojeikuaa mba'éichapa oikóva opaichagua mba'e rehe.
Oñe'ẽ 'down' rehe oñeikotevẽva mba'e oiko haguéva.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Excuse me, can you help me? I need to get off at the next stop.
dialogue.translation: Ahendu, ¿nde porãite oñepytyvõta? Ne'ẽ ko'ápe oiko tapykuepe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sure. Which stop do you want? This is the next stop.
dialogue.translation: Ko'ỹte. ¿Máva tapykue ndereko? Ko'ápe oiko tapykuepe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want the stop near the hospital. How many stops from here?
dialogue.translation: Ndeheko tapykue yvypópe. ¿Mba'éichapa oiko tapykue ko'ápe?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It's three stops down. Please sit down, I will tell you.
dialogue.translation: Mbohapy tapykue yvy'a. Porãite, ndéve ahecha.

key_phrases.phrase: get off at the next stop

scenario: Introducing a colleague at work
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha haĝua ojeiko haguépe ojejapo haguéicha.
Ko ápe, 'meet' oñehenói haĝua 'conocer' por primera vez.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hello, this is our new colleague. Her name is Ana.
dialogue.translation: Mba'éichapa, ko ápe oñehenói ñande rova. Héra Ana.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nice to meet you, Ana. What do you do here?
dialogue.translation: Jajapo ndéve, Ana. Mba'éichapa ndéiko ko ápe?

dialogue.speaker: C
dialogue.text: She works in our team. He is her manager.
dialogue.translation: Ha'e oñemba'apo ñande aty. Ha'e héra ñande mburuvicha.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Good! I want to work with you.
dialogue.translation: Porã! Aha'ãicha ndéve oñemba'apo.

scenario: Leaving a voicemail message
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hello, this is Ana. Please leave a message after the beep.
dialogue.translation: Mba'éichapa, ndéva Ana. Eñe'ẽ mba'erepy kuarahy rire pitido.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hi Ana, this is Luis. Please call me back soon.
dialogue.translation: Mba'éichapa Ana, ndéva Luis. Eñe'ẽ jevy ndéve mbegue.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Okay, Luis. What is your number?
dialogue.translation: Ha'eve, Luis. Mba'eichapa nde ñemohu?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: It is 555-1234. Thank you!

scenario: At the post office sending a package
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: En este contexto, 'have' se usa como verbo auxiliar en presente perfecto

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I want to send this package to my friend.
dialogue.translation: Aha upéa che amigo-pe paquete ojehechávo.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We have it at the counter. Please fill out this form for the package.
dialogue.translation: Ñande oiko péicha. Ha upéicha ojejapo kóva formulario paquete-pe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Is this all for the package?
dialogue.translation: Kóva opa pa? Paquete-pe?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, we have all we need. You can send it now.
dialogue.translation: Heta, ñande oiko mbarete. Upéicha ojehechávo ko'ápe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Thank you.
dialogue.translation: Aguijey.

scenario: Describing your daily routine
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I get up at seven in the morning.
dialogue.translation: Ajyhy peteĩ ára pyhareve.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I have breakfast and go to work.
dialogue.translation: Upéi añembi'u tembi'u pyhareve ha aha trabajo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I work at home in the evening.
dialogue.translation: Aha trabajo og̃ape ka'aru.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I watch TV because I like it.
dialogue.translation: Ahecha televisión porã che ndaikuaái.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Then I sleep at ten.
dialogue.translation: Upéi ake peteĩ ára.

scenario: Asking about opening hours
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ojehecha haguã umi tembiapo oñemoĩmbarete haguã oiko público-pe.
Oñe’ẽ haguã tembiapo oñembo’o, ápe oñe’ẽ oiko presente-pe.
Ápe oñe’ẽ haguã ñe’ẽ ojehecháicha ojejapo tembiapo ojehecháicha.
Oñe’ẽ haguã tembiapo ojehecháicha ojeikuaa haguã.
Oñe’ẽ haguã tembiapo oñe’ẽ oñe’ẽ oñe’ẽ oñe’ẽ.
Oñe’ẽ haguã tembiapo oñe’ẽ oñe’ẽ oñe’ẽ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you tell me the open time today?
dialogue.translation: ¿Puedes decirme la hora de apertura hoy?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We open at nine, but we close at five.
dialogue.translation: Abrimos a las nueve, pero cerramos a las cinco.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: And on Saturday, until what time are you open?
dialogue.translation: ¿Y el sábado, hasta qué hora estáis abiertos?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: On Saturday, we close at one.
dialogue.translation: El sábado, cerramos a la una.

scenario: Choosing a dish from a menu
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What do you like to eat?
dialogue.translation: Mba’épa rejeréko?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I like fish or chicken with rice.
dialogue.translation: Ajuhu pescado o pollo con arroz.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The fish is very good here.
dialogue.translation: Upéva pescado oï mba’eeté porã.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I try some fish, please.
dialogue.translation: Upéi ajuhu mba’éicha pescado, por favor.

key_phrases.phrase: What do you like to eat?
The fish is very good here.

scenario: At the bank for a simple transaction
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Ñe’ẽ oikóva ojehechávo determinante ('etéva dinero') ha ojehechávo adverbio ('etéva rire').

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I need money now.
dialogue.translation: Nde ne’ẽ dinero ápe.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Here is your card. Go there with your ID.
dialogue.translation: Akuápe ha’ã nde tarjeta. Ha’ã upépe ndive nde cédula.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will you give me more cash?
dialogue.translation: Nde oime’ẽ etéva efectivo?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I will give you the money now. Go there.
dialogue.translation: Héi, aháme’ẽ nde dinero ápe. Ha’ã upépe.
